TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r2.claim: The Qur’an contrasts what perishes with what endures, teaching that what is with God is better and lasting.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r2.anchor: ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r4.claim: This passage reassures the Prophet and answers Quraysh's fear that accepting the call would destroy their political and economic influence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r4.anchor: The Prophet (sws) is given assurance and an answer is given to the Quraysh to allay their fear

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p316/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p316/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p316/r5.claim: Pleasant, boast-worthy gifts are brief worldly enjoyment and ornament; God's enduring bliss for believers is better, and the question rebukes them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p316/r5.anchor: وما أوتيتم من شيء: أي حسن يسركم وتفخرون به، فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p316/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p316/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p316/r6.claim: Abu Amr reads يعقلون with yāʾ to address others and expose poor judgment; the majority use ta to address and rebuke them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p316/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: يعقلون، بالياء، إعراض عن خطابهم وخطاب لغيرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p316/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p316/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p316/r7.claim: A variant متاعا الحياة الدنيا makes life a time adverb, meaning they enjoy themselves during worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p316/r7.anchor: وقرىء: متاعا الحياة الدنيا، أي يمتعون متاعا في الحياة الدنيا

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p559/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p559/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p559/r2.claim: Addressing Quraysh's leaders directly, the author contrasts their brief worldly luxury with God's better, lasting reward for those who seek the Hereafter, urging them not to squander it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p559/r2.anchor: The previous warnings were indirect. This verse directly addresses the leaders of the Quraysh.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

SAMIN-DURR:28:60/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:60/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:60/r1.claim: The nominative فمتاع means فهو متاع; a variant accusative parses as a verbal noun, with الحياة as a temporal accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:28:60/r1.anchor: قوله: { فمتاع }: أي: فهو متاع. وقرىء " فمتاعا الحياة " بنصب " متاعا " على المصدر أي: يتمتعون متاعا،

SAMIN-DURR:28:60/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:60/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:28:60/r2.claim: Abu Amr reads تعقلون with third-person ياء as a shift in address; others retain direct address in context.
SAMIN-DURR:28:60/r2.anchor: قوله: { تعقلون } قرأ أبو عمرو بالياء من تحت التفاتا. والباقون بالخطاب جريا على ما تقدم.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p548/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p548/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p548/r2.claim: The mission concludes the truth for Quraysh, so they cannot claim ignorance if punishment comes after the warning.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p424/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p424/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p424/r1.claim: Abu Amr alone reads the verb with yāʾ as yaʿqilūn; the other readers use tāʾ as taʿqilūn.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p424/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحده: (أفلا يعقلون) وتعقلون بالتاء والياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p424/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p424/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p424/r2.claim: The tāʾ reading keeps the discourse in one second-person mode after وما أوتيتم; the yāʾ reading asks Muhammad whether they understand.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p424/r2.anchor: حجة التاء قوله: وما أوتيتم من شيء أفلا تعقلون

QIRAAT-ER:28:60:21#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:60:21#1/r1.speaker: Imp
QIRAAT-ER:28:60:21#1/r1.claim: The third-person yaʿqilūna (“will they reason?”) shifts from direct address to commentary about an absent group, changing confrontation into observation.
QIRAAT-ER:28:60:21#1/r1.anchor: Imp, mutawatir: "Shift from 2nd person (تَعْقِلُونَ, ""will you not reason?"") to 3rd person (يَعْقِلُونَ

ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r1.claim: Anything people attain among worldly affairs and means is a temporary use and adornment; matāʿ signals brevity, the contrast with abqā stresses it, and dunyā suggests lowliness and short duration.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r1.anchor: فهو شيء شأنه أن يتمتع به ويتزين به أياما قلائل ويشعر بالقلة لفظ المتاع

ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r2.claim: What is with God means the reward in Paradise; it is intrinsically better as pure pleasure and complete joy, and more lasting because eternal, unlike the finite world.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r3.claim: The question urges reflection on the obvious choice: do not trade the lower for the better, fear losing worldly possessions, and refuse guidance that leads to God's reward based on that hypothetical fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r3.anchor: أي ألا تتفكرون فلا تفعلون هذا الأمر الواضح فتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads yaʿqilūn in the third person; the shift makes the admonition stronger by implying that they are too senseless to merit direct address.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو يعقلون بياء الغيبة على الالتفات وهو أبلغ في الموعظة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r5.claim: A variant reads matāʿan in the accusative as a verbal noun and al-ḥayāta as a temporal adverb, meaning they enjoy it in worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p98#3/r5.anchor: وقريء ( فمتاعا الحياة الدنيا ) أي فتتمتعون به في الحياة الدنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p216#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p216#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p216#2/r4.claim: Worldly possessions provide enjoyment only during life, then perish; what is with God is better and more enduring, since what lasts is better than what passes.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p216#2/r4.anchor: تتمتعون بها أيام حياتكم ثم هي إلى فناء وانقضاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p216#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p216#2/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p216#2/r5.claim: Most readers use second-person ta in تعقلون; Abu ʿAmr permits either ta or ya.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p216#2/r5.anchor: قرأ عامة القراء: "تعقلون" بالتاء وأبو عمرو بالخيار بين التاء والياء

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r1.claim: The gifts mentioned are worldly means.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r1.anchor: { وما أوتيتم من شيء } من أسباب الدنيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r2.claim: Worldly means provide enjoyment and adornment only during this finite life.

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r3.claim: What is with God refers to His reward.

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r4.claim: God's reward is better as complete delight and pleasure, and more enduring because everlasting.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r4.anchor: { خير } في نفسه من ذلك لأنه لذة خاصة

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r5.claim: The question urges people to exchange the lower worldly good for what is better.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r5.anchor: فتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r6.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads with yāʾ, making the admonition more emphatic.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بالياء وهو أبلغ في الموعظة

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r11.claim: The following verse concludes the previous one and is joined to it with faʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:60-61/r11.anchor: وهذه الآية كالنتيجة للتي قبلها ولذلك رتبت عليها بالفاء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r1.claim: Everything people receive is temporary enjoyment of worldly life, whose benefit ends here even if it lasts a long time.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r2.claim: The world and all its adornments are neither eternal in the past nor everlasting in the future.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r2.anchor: وهو زينة الحياة الدنيا التي هي كلها فضلا عن زينتها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r3.claim: The reward promised for obedience belongs to the afterlife, which the description of this life as near and low implies.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r3.anchor: مما تثمره لكم المتابعة من الثواب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r4.claim: God’s promise of reward is wholly trustworthy.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r5.claim: Even if people imagine worldly pleasure shares in goodness, what God has is greater, more pleasant, beautiful, and satisfying.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r5.anchor: لأن الذي عنده أكثر وأطيب وأظهر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r6.claim: The afterlife is everlasting, though it was not eternal in the past, whereas worldly pleasure ends.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r6.anchor: لأنه وإن شارك متاع الدنيا في أنه بم يكن

BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r7.claim: The question rebukes anyone who avoids the peril of obedience by choosing the greater peril of disobedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p508/r7.anchor: فلما بان أنه لا يقدم على خطر المخالفة المذكور خوفا من خطر المتابعة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r1.speaker: سفيان
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r1.claim: Sufyān says the world is called al-dunyā because it is near.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r1.anchor: سمعت سفيان ، يقول : انما سميت الدنيا ، لانها دنت

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r2.speaker: عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh urges whoever can to place their treasure where moth cannot eat it and thieves cannot reach it.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r2.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة بن عبد الله قال : قال عبد الله : من استطاع منكم ان يضع كنزه حيث لا ياكله السوس

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r3.speaker: كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r3.claim: Kaʿb says the Torah promises that treasure deposited with God is safe from flood and fire and will be returned on the Day of Resurrection when it is most needed.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r3.anchor: عن كعب قال : مكتوب في التوراة : ابن ادم ضع كنزك ، عندي ، فلا غرق ولا حرق ادفعه اليك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r4.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd urges people to send worldly provision ahead to the afterlife, where they will find what they sent from God's provision.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r4.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم يقول : لا تنسى ان تقدم من دنياك لاخرتك فانما تجد في اخرتك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses do you not reason as do you not reflect.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2998/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله : افلا تعقلون قال : افلا تتفكرون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r3.claim: The verse follows the reminder of Meccan security and provision: worldly goods are temporary, while the afterlife is better and enduring, so believers should seek it through faith even if guidance costs them worldly advantages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r3.anchor: هذا وجه مناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r4.claim: Min shayʾ clarifies the general “whatever you have been given”; the context makes the referent beneficial things, since giving commonly means granting what benefits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r4.anchor: و { من شيء } بيان ل { ما أوتيتم } والمراد من أشياء المنافع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r5.claim: The wording shifts from speaking of them in the third person to addressing them directly because the preceding speech calls for face-to-face reproach.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r5.anchor: وقد التفت الكلام من الغيبة من قوله { أو لم نمكن لهم حرما } ( القصص : 57 ) إلى الخطاب في قوله { أوتيتم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r6.claim: Matāʿ is something enjoyed for a time and then lost.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r6.anchor: والمتاع : ما ينتفع به زمنا ثم يزول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r7.claim: Zīna means what makes bodies or things beautiful.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r8.claim: The afterlife is better in the quality and completeness of its kinds of blessings, and more enduring because it is everlasting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r8.anchor: أن أجناس الآخرة خير مما أوتوه في كمال أجناسها ، وأما كونه أبقى فهو بمعنى الخلود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r9.claim: The closing question reproaches them and presses them to acknowledge their failure to use sound reason, treating them as if their minds were impaired.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p153/r9.anchor: وتفرع على هذا الخبر استفهام توبيخي وتقريري على عدم عقل المخاطبين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p154/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p154/r1.speaker: الجمهور; أبو عمرو ويعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p154/r1.claim: Most readers have taʿqilūn with second-person tāʾ; Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb read yaʿqilūn with third-person yāʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p154/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { تعقلون } بتاء الخطاب . وقرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب { يعقلون } بياء الغيبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p154/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p154/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p154/r2.claim: The third-person reading may turn from direct address so believers marvel at the polytheists, or treat them as absent because their lack of reason puts them far from direct address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p154/r2.anchor: على الالتفات عن خطابهم لتعجب المؤمنين من حالهم ، وقيل : لأنهم لما كانوا لا يعقلون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p154/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p154/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p154/r3.claim: The author thinks the connective fa introduces the contrast because polytheists flaunted wealth and luxury while most Muslims were poor; the transient worldly lot contrasts with the believers’ lasting reward and the disbelievers’ punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p154/r3.anchor: أحسب أن موقع فاء التفريع هنا أن مما أومأ إليه قوله { وما أوتيتم من شيء

BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r1.claim: The first mā is a subject carrying a conditional sense, which accounts for the fāʾ in its predicate; the following mā is different.
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r1.anchor: {وما} مبتدأ متضمنة لمعنى الشرط لدخول الفاء في خبرها بخلاف الثانية

BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r2.speaker: الوسيط
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r2.claim: The address is to Meccan disbelievers, and the gifts are worldly means.
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r2.anchor: أعطيتم والخطاب لكفار مكة كما في "الوسيط"

BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r3.claim: Worldly gifts are brief means for enjoyment and adornment that soon perish, like household goods; they are called mataʿ because they do not last.
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r3.anchor: أي : فهو شيء شأنه أن يتمتع ويتزين به أياما قلائل

BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r4.claim: What is with God is reward, better in itself because its pleasure is free of pain and worry, and more lasting because it is eternal.

BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r5.claim: The question urges reflection: why trade the inferior, fleeting life and misery from disbelief and sin for the better reward and happiness of faith and obedience?
BURSEVI:v6p304#2/r5.anchor: ألا تتفكرون فلا تعقلون هذا الأمر الواضح فتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p293#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p293#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p293#2/r4.claim: Addressing Quraysh, God belittles their pride in wealth, sons, and strength: these are perishable worldly goods, while the believers' Hereafter is better and more lasting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p293#2/r4.anchor: ثم خاطب تعالى قريشا محقرا لما كانوا يفخرون به من مال وبنين وغير ذلك من قوة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p293#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p293#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p293#2/r5.claim: Most read يعقلون in third person; Abu Amr is also reported with that reading, though a report gives him second person.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p293#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p293#2/r6.speaker: أبو علي وأبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p293#2/r6.claim: Abu Ali says Abu Amr's report conflicts with Abu Hatim and others, who say Nafi reads second person, as do al-Araj, Hasan, and Isa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p293#2/r6.anchor: وذلك خلاف ما حكى أبو حاتم والناس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p234/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p234/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p234/r1.claim: Whatever wealth or good people receive is worldly enjoyment during their lives, then it fades and passes away.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p234/r1.anchor: وما أوتيتم من شئ أي ما أعطيتم من مال وخير فمتاع الحياة الدنيا تتمتعون به ايام حياتكم ثم يفنى وينقضي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p234/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p234/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p234/r2.claim: God’s reward is better and more enduring for its recipients; reason should recognize that what lasts is better than what perishes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p234/r2.anchor: وما عند الله من الثواب خير وأبقى أفضل وأدوم لأهله أفلا تعقلون ان الباقي أفضل من الفاني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r1.claim: Worldly adornment is lowly and fleeting beside the immense, lasting bliss God has prepared for the righteous in the Hereafter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى مخبرا عن حقارة الدنيا (1) ، وما فيها من الزينة الدنيئة والزهرة الفانية بالنسبة إلى ما أعده الله لعباده الصالحين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir links the contrast to verses saying what is with God remains, is better for the righteous, and that the Hereafter is better and more lasting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r2.anchor: كما قال: {ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق} [النحل: 96] ، وقال: {وما عند الله خير للأبرار}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r3.claim: The Prophet likens this world compared with the Hereafter to a finger dipped into the sea and what it brings back.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r3.anchor: "والله ما الدنيا في الآخرة، إلا كما يغمس أحدكم إصبعه في اليم، فلينظر ماذا يرجع إليه"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r4.claim: The question asks whether people reason when they prefer the present world to the Hereafter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249/r4.anchor: أي: أفلا يعقل من يقدم الدنيا على الآخرة؟

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p429/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p429/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p429/r1.claim: Whatever worldly means people receive is only brief enjoyment and adornment for a finite life; God's reward is better and lasts forever.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p429/r1.anchor: وأي شيء أصبتموه من أسباب الدنيا فما هو إلا تمتع وزينة أياما قلائل ، وهي مدة الحياة المتقضية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p429/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p429/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p429/r2.claim: A reading with third-person يَعقلون is more forceful as a warning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p429/r2.anchor: وقرىء : ( يعقلون ) بالياء ، وهو أبلغ في الموعظة .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p429/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p429/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p429/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God made three classes in the world: believers provision for the next life, hypocrites adorn themselves, and disbelievers simply enjoy worldly life.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p429/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن الله خلق الدنيا وجعل أهلها ثلاثة أصناف : المؤمن ، والمنافق ، والكافر

MUQATIL:28:60-61/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:60-61/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:60-61/r1.claim: Whatever good the Meccan unbelievers receive is only worldly provision and adornment during their lifetimes, and it will pass away.
MUQATIL:28:60-61/r1.anchor: وما أوتيتم من شيء } يقول: وما أعطيتم من خير، يعنى به كفار مكة { فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها

MUQATIL:28:60-61/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:60-61/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:60-61/r2.claim: God's reward is better and more lasting for its people than the fading things given in this world.
MUQATIL:28:60-61/r2.anchor: وما عند الله } من الثواب { خير وأبقى } يعنى أفضل وأدوم لأهله مما أعطيتم في الدنيا

MUQATIL:28:60-61/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:60-61/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:60-61/r3.claim: People should understand that what lasts is better than what vanishes.
MUQATIL:28:60-61/r3.anchor: أفلا تعقلون } [آية: 60] أن الباقي خير من الفاني الذاهب.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r1.claim: Whatever worldly means people acquire is enjoyment and adornment for a few days, the short span of mortal life.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r1.anchor: وأي شيء أصبتموه من أسباب الدنيا فما هو إلا تمتع وزينة أياما قلائل وهي مدة الحياة الفانية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r2.claim: What is with God is His reward, better in itself and enduring.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r2.anchor: وهو ثوابه ﴿ خير ﴾ في نفسه من ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r3.claim: The verse asks whether people understand that what lasts is better than what perishes.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r4.claim: Abu Amr reads the verb with ya, while the other readers use ta.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r4.anchor: أبو عمرو وبين الياء والتاء والباقون بالتاء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says worldly people are three classes: the believer stores provisions, the hypocrite adorns himself, and the disbeliever enjoys life.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p242#3/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن الله تعالى خلق الدنيا وجعل أهلها ثلاثة أصناف المؤمن والنافق والكافر

QURTUBI-FULL:28:59-61/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:59-61/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:59-61/r8.claim: Addressing Meccans, al-Qurtubi says all they receive is worldly enjoyment and adornment, lasting only part of life before they or it depart.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:59-61/r8.anchor: أي تتمتعون بها مدة حياتكم، أو مدة في حياتكم،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:59-61/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:59-61/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:59-61/r9.claim: What is with God is better and more enduring: the afterlife, meaning Paradise; reason should recognize that what lasts is better than what fades.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:59-61/r9.anchor: أي أفضل وأدوم، يريد الدار الآخرة وهي الجنة. { أفلا تعقلون } أن الباقي أفضل من الفاني.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:59-61/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:59-61/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:28:59-61/r10.claim: Abu Amr reads yaʿqilūn in the third person; the other readers use the second person, which al-Qurtubi prefers because the preceding phrase addresses the audience.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:59-61/r10.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو: { يعقلون } بالياء. الباقون بالتاء على الخطاب وهو الاختيار

RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r1.claim: This is the third answer to the opponents’ claim that they abandoned religion to avoid losing worldly life: what God has is better and more lasting.
RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أن هذا هو الجواب الثالث : عن تلك الشبهة لأن حاصل شبهتهم أن قالوا تركنا الدين لئلا تفوتنا الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r2.claim: The afterlife is better because its benefits are greater and free of the harms mixed into worldly benefits, where harms predominate.
RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r2.anchor: أما أنه خير فلوجهين أحدهما : أن المنافع هناك أعظم وثانيهما : أنها خالصة عن الشوائب

RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r3.claim: The afterlife lasts because it is permanent, whereas worldly benefits end; compared with the infinite, the finite is as nothing, and each person’s worldly share is tiny beside the whole.
RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r3.anchor: أما أنها أبقى فلأنها دائمة غير منقطعة ومنافع الدنيا منقطعة ومتى قوبل المتناهي بغير المتناهي كان عدما

RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r4.claim: Choosing worldly benefits over the greater afterlife benefits is a grave failure of reason; al-Shafi‘i says a bequest to the most intelligent should go to those devoted to obedience, who give little and gain much.
RAZI-FULL:v25p6#2/r4.anchor: ورحم الله الشافعي حيث قال : من أوصى بثلث ماله لأعقل الناس صرف ذلك الثلث إلى المشتغلين بطاعة الله

STUDYQURAN:28:60/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:60/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:60/r1.claim: The world's inferiority to the enduring Hereafter, or what lies with God, is a major Quranic theme.
STUDYQURAN:28:60/r1.anchor: The inferiority of this transient world in comparison with the more enduring Hereafter or with what lies with God is a major theme of the Quran

STUDYQURAN:28:60/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:60/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:28:60/r2.claim: R compares this world to a speck of dust beside the sea and says the Hereafter endures forever while this world ends.
STUDYQURAN:28:60/r2.anchor: this world in relation to the Hereafter is like a speck of dust in relation to the sea

STUDYQURAN:28:60/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:60/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:60/r3.claim: The idea of worldly goods as ornament also appears in 33:28.
STUDYQURAN:28:60/r3.anchor: The idea of the goods of this world as an ornament is also mentioned in 33:28

TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r1.claim: Whatever wealth or children people receive is only a worldly enjoyment and adornment; it cannot benefit them with God or in the return to Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r1.anchor: لا يغني عنكم عند الله شيئا، ولا ينفعكم شيء منه في معادكم

TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r2.claim: What God keeps for those who obey and remain loyal to Him is better than worldly provision and lasts forever without depletion.
TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r2.anchor: وما عند الله لأهل طاعته وولايته خير مما أوتيتموه أنتم في هذه الدنيا من متاعها وزينتها وأبقى، يقول: وأبقى لأهله

TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq glosses God’s reward as better in recompense and more enduring.
TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، في قوله " {وما عند الله خير وأبقى} [القصص: 60] قال: خير ثوابا، وأبقى عندنا

TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r4.claim: The rebuke asks whether people can reason well enough to distinguish good from evil and choose lasting bliss over the perishing, lesser alternative.
TAB-FULL:v18p292#2/r4.anchor: أفلا عقول لكم أيها القوم تتدبرون بها فتعرفون بها الخير من الشر، وتختارون لأنفسكم خير المنزلتين على شرهما

SULAMI:v2p108/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p108/r1.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v2p108/r1.claim: All creatures worship blessings; rare and precious is the one who worships the Benefactor. Whoever is separated from God by anything is cheated, even if the separation comes through obedience or Paradise.
SULAMI:v2p108/r1.anchor: قال النصرآباذي : الخلق كلهم عبدة النعم والغريب والعزيز فيهم من يعبد المنعم

SULAMI:v2p108/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p108/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p108/r2.claim: The first statement addresses ordinary people; the elect are told that God is better and more enduring.

TUSTARI:28:60/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:28:60/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:28:60/r1.claim: Taking worldly goods out of desire deprives one of better things in this life and the next: the pleasure of worship and love of God here, and the highest ranks hereafter.
TUSTARI:28:60/r1.anchor: من أخذ من الدنيا بشهوة منه حرمه الله في الدنيا والآخرة ما هو خير منها

TUSTARI:28:60/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:28:60/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:28:60/r2.claim: Taking what is needed because of personal compulsion or an obligation one must fulfill does not deprive one of what is better.
TUSTARI:28:60/r2.anchor: ومن أخذ منها لضرورة دخلت بنفسه أو لحق لزمه لم يحرم ما هو خير في الدنيا

TUSTARI:28:60/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:28:60/r3.speaker: عامر بن عبد قيس
TUSTARI:28:60/r3.claim: When told he was content with little worldly provision, ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Qays said that one is even less content if one accepts the world as one's share of the hereafter.
TUSTARI:28:60/r3.anchor: وقيل لعامر بن عبد قيس: لقد رضيت من الدنيا باليسير

TABATABAI:28:59-61/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r2.claim: إيتاء means giving; من شيء clarifies ما and generalizes it to everything given. متاع is what one enjoys, and زينة is an addition that beautifies something.
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r2.anchor: الإيتاء الإعطاء و { من شيء } بيان لما لإفادة العموم

TABATABAI:28:59-61/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r3.claim: The lower life is deferred and finite, nearer to people than the other life; it contrasts with the eternal afterlife.
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r3.anchor: الحياة الدنيا الحياة المؤجلة المقطوعة التي هي أقرب الحياتين منا

TABATABAI:28:59-61/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r4.claim: What is with God means the blessed afterlife in His presence, described as better and more lasting.
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r4.anchor: والمراد بما عند الله الحياة الآخرة السعيدة التي عند الله وجواره ولذا عد خيرا وأبقى

TABATABAI:28:59-61/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r5.claim: All worldly gifts are transient enjoyment and adornment, while God’s reward for following guidance and believing His signs is better and lasting, so it should be preferred.
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r5.anchor: جميع النعم الدنيوية التي أعطاكم الله إياها متاع وزينة زينت بها هذه الحياة الدنيا

TABATABAI:28:59-61/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r6.claim: This is a third answer to the fear of being seized from their land: even conceding that danger, they would lose only fleeting worldly adornment, not the better lasting reward of guidance.
TABATABAI:28:59-61/r6.anchor: والآية جواب ثالث عن قولهم { إن نتبع الهدى معك نتخطف من أرضنا }

TABRISI:28:58-60/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:58-60/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:58-60/r11.claim: Whatever people receive is worldly enjoyment and adornment; God’s reward and the afterlife are better and more enduring because worldly goods perish.

TABRISI:28:58-60/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:58-60/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:58-60/r12.claim: The closing question urges reflection to distinguish what lasts from what passes away.

THALABI:v7p255/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p255/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p255/r12.claim: Whatever people receive is only the enjoyment and adornment of worldly life; what God has is better and more enduring, so people should reason.
THALABI:v7p255/r12.anchor: وما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها وما عند الله خير وأبقى أفلا تعقلون

THALABI:v7p255/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p255/r13.speaker: أبو عمرو
THALABI:v7p255/r13.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads the verb with yāʾ: ‘Do they not reason?’

THALABI:v7p255/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p255/r14.speaker: الباقون
THALABI:v7p255/r14.claim: The other readers use tāʾ: ‘Will you not reason?’

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r1.claim: The address is to Meccan unbelievers: whatever wealth or good they receive is worldly enjoyment and adornment that ends with their lives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل: يعني كفار مكة، يقول: ما أعطيتم من خير ومال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r2.claim: God's reward and bliss for believers are better and more lasting for their recipients than worldly gifts; the enduring outweighs the transient.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r2.anchor: من الثواب والنعيم للمؤمنين {خير وأبقى} أفضل وأدوم لأهله مما أعطيتم في الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r3.claim: They ask whether people understand that what lasts is better than what vanishes.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the verb in the third person, do they not understand?
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r4.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو: {أفلا يعقلون} بالياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p431#2/r5.claim: On the third-person reading, the question addresses Muhammad: do they not understand this?

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:60/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:60/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:60/r1.claim: The address to Meccan polytheists contrasts their temporary worldly enjoyments with God's better, enduring afterlife gifts; verse 62 then compares the groups who receive them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:60/r1.anchor: Mekke müşriklerine hitap edilerek onların sahip olduğu dünya nimet ve ziynetlerinin geçici, Allah’ın âhirette vereceği nimetlerin ise daha hayırlı ve kalıcı olduğu ifade edilmekte

BURHAN:v1p128/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p128/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p128/r4.claim: The Shura wording begins with fa, unlike the waw in al-Qasas; it is one of the cited examples of substituting one particle for another.
BURHAN:v1p128/r4.anchor: فى القصص ﴿ وما أوتيتم من شيء ﴾ وفى الشورى ﴿ فما أوتيتم ﴾ بالفاء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r5.claim: Baqiyyah can mean permanence: what is with God endures, and what is with people passes away.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r5.anchor: والثاني : الدوام ، ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p603/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p603/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p603/r8.claim: What people receive is transient worldly enjoyment and adornment; what is with God is Paradise.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p603/r8.anchor: قوله عز وجل:} وما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها وما عند الله خير وأبقى { [القصص: 60] الجنة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p603/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p603/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p603/r9.claim: The admonition to reason is addressed to the polytheists.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r14.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r14.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r14.claim: Al-Qasas mentions adornment because Qarun later appears before his people in it; al-Shura has no comparable worldly scene, so the addition suits the former context.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r14.anchor: وقد ورد ذكر الزينة في القصص لورودها فيما بعد

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r15.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r15.speaker: معترك الأقران
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r15.claim: Ma‘tarak al-aqran likewise connects the added adornment to Qarun’s story, where it makes the verse fit the narrative; al-Shura contains no such worldly episode.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p493/r10.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p493/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p493/r10.claim: Abu ʿAmr alone reads both أفلا تعقلون and أفلا يعقلون, with tāʾ and yāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p493/r10.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحده ﴿ أفلا تعقلون ﴾ و ﴿ أفلا يعقلون ﴾ بالتاء والياء

NASHR:v2p342/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p342/r2.speaker: الدوري عن أبي عمرو
NASHR:v2p342/r2.claim: Al-Dūrī, transmitting from Abū ʿAmr, reads أفلا تعقلون in the third person; many authorities also fix this for al-Sūsī, and al-Dānī and others prefer it.
NASHR:v2p342/r2.anchor: أفلا تعقلون، فروى الدوري عن أبي عمرو بالغيب، واختلف عن السوسي عنه،

NASHR:v2p342/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p342/r3.speaker: أبو طاهر بن سوار وأبو العلاء
NASHR:v2p342/r3.claim: Ibn Sawwār and Abū al-ʿAlāʾ fix the second-person address for al-Sūsī; other authorities allow both forms equally for him and al-Dūrī.
NASHR:v2p342/r3.anchor: وقطع له آخرون بالخطاب كالأستاذ أبي طاهر بن سوار والحافظ أبي العلاء،

NASHR:v2p342/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p342/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p342/r4.claim: The author accepts both forms through the cited routes but says the third person is more famous; he uses both with al-Sūsī, while the remaining readers use direct address.
NASHR:v2p342/r4.anchor: والوجهان صحيحان عن أبي عمرو من هذه الطرق، وغيرهما إلا أن الأشهر عنه بالغيب،
